prompt: Fraud committed over the internet has increased significantly in recent years. Why has this type of crime become so common? What can individuals do to protect themselves?
essay:
The growth of online fraud is usually blamed on gullibility, which gets the causation backwards. What has changed is not the credulity of victims but the economics of the crime, and understanding that is what tells an individual where their own effort is worth spending.

Three things have shifted at once. The information required to impersonate somebody is now published as a matter of course, scattered across retailers, employers and social networks, so an offender begins with material that once took weeks of work to assemble. The act itself has become almost costless to attempt: a fraudulent message can be sent to a hundred thousand people for the price of nothing, which means a success rate of one in ten thousand is still a business. And enforcement has not kept pace, because a crime originating in one jurisdiction, harming somebody in a second and laundered through a third is nobody's clear responsibility, while individual losses are usually too small to trigger the effort required.

Taken together, those three facts describe a crime attempted at industrial volume against targets chosen for convenience rather than for wealth. That is the useful insight, because it means an individual is not trying to become uncrackable — only more expensive to attack than the next person on the list.

Three habits achieve most of that. Two-factor authentication converts a stolen password from a key into a useless string, which defeats the commonest attack outright. A password manager ensures that a breach at one careless retailer does not hand over an email account as well. Most importantly, treat urgency itself as the warning sign: virtually every successful fraud requires its victim to act before they think, so the discipline of ending any unexpected call or message and making contact independently, through a number you already had, removes the pressure the whole method depends on. None of these is difficult, and that is the point — the defences that work are the ones a person will still be using in a year.
title: Why online fraud keeps growing
